subject: United States
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Alaska Purchase. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). Russia is a flagged country in the map data (Crimea, Kuril Islands; none shown); it is outlined only as the seller, so the episode needs the borders review before release.

claims.text: The Alaska Purchase in 1867 resulted in the transfer of Russian America to the United States for $7.2 million.
At an original cost of $0.02 per acre, the United States had grown by 586,412 square miles (1,518,800 km²).
On April 9, 1867, the U.S. Senate ratified the treaty signed on March 30; American sovereignty became legally effective on October 18.
Opponents labelled the purchase "Seward’s Folly" or "Seward’s Icebox".
Alexander II of Russia, having faced a catastrophic defeat in the Crimean War, began exploring the possibility of selling Alaska, which would be difficult to defend in any future war.
